encyclopedia.summary: Valve's 1998 first-person shooter, built on the GoldSrc engine. After an experiment tears a hole into another dimension, the theoretical physicist Gordon Freeman walks out of the research facility without saying a word. It is remembered for telling a story without cutscenes, keeping the camera in his eyes and the space unbroken.

key_facts.value: Windows, macOS and Linux in the current release

highlights: Tells its story in first person without a single spoken line from the lead.
Unbroken spaces and scripted scenes gave the shooter a narrative.
Its mod scene produced Counter-Strike and Team Fortress.

encyclopedia.summary: A first-person shooter made by MachineGames in 2014, set in the 1960s of a world where Nazi Germany won the Second World War. B.J. Blazkowicz wakes from a coma and fights again with a resistance. It reboots the series while keeping the original's mechanical weapons and occult trappings.

key_facts.value: First game of the Wolfenstein reboot

highlights: It moves between 1946 and the 1960s to set the same man's choices side by side.
Dual-wielding different guns shapes the rhythm of every fight.
The cutscenes are longer and more serious than the genre usually allows.

related.note: The follow-up with the same lead

encyclopedia.summary: A first-person shooter made by Monolith Productions in 2005, set after a corporation's paranormal experiments get out of control. Gunfire has real weight, and the visions appearing in corridors and offices do the horror. Its slow-motion ability and the enemies' evasive AI were what reviews focused on at the time.
highlights: Enemies choose cover and flanking on their own, and that is the core of the combat.
The horror comes from repeated spaces and sound rather than from jump scares.
Slow motion turns a firefight into something close to an edited film.

related.note: A first-person shooter from the same year that set the bar for spatial staging
A later supernatural shooter set in a research facility
A first-person shooter built on the feel of its weapons
